title: Ukrainian officials to boycott Paralympics after Russian competitors reinstated
content:
Ukraine’s state representatives are refusing to participate in the 2026 Paralympic Games after Russian athletes were awarded six slots to compete under their own flag.

The International Paralympic Committee confirmed on Tuesday that Russian and Belarusians would be able to represent for their own countries for the first time since 2014. Russian participants at the Olympics in Milan Cortina have been competing neutrally.

Russian athletes have not been able to compete under their flag since 2016, when Canadian legal professor Dr. Richard McLaren released his report into state-sanctioned doping in the nation.

The IPC and IOC then maintained a suspension over Russia after the country’s invasion of Ukraine in 2022, with the conflict ongoing. The Ukrainian minister of youth and sports Matvii Bidnyi then announced Wednesday that his country’s officials will not be participating in any official events at the Paralympics, beginning with the opening ceremony on March 6.

“In response to the Paralympics organisers’ outrageous decision to let Russians and Belarusians compete under their national flags, Ukrainian public officials will not attend the Paralympic Games,” Bidnyi said on his social media.

“We will not be present at the opening ceremony. We will not take part in any other official Paralympic events.

“We thank every official from the free world who will do the same. We will keep fighting!”

The statement was then reaffirmed by the Ministry of Youth and Sports’ social media.

The European commissioner for intergenerational fairness, youth, culture and sport Glenn Micallef also confirmed he would not attend the opening ceremony, calling the return of Russia “unacceptable”.

“While Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine continues, I cannot support the reinstatement of national symbols, flags, anthems and uniforms, that are inseparable from that conflict,” he added.

It is not the first time that Ukraine government officials have spoken out against the Games’ organisation.

President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said last week “the Olympic movement should help stop wars, not play into the hands of aggressors” after skeleton racer Vladyslav Heraskevych was not allowed to compete due to his “helmet of remembrance”.

The IOC ruled that Herskevych’s helmet, which depicted Ukrainian athletes who had died in the conflict, violated its rules of political expression on the field of play and he could not participate with it on.

On Tuesday, Rinat Akhmetov — the president of the country’s biggest soccer club, Shakhtar Donetsk — donated more than $231,096 to encourage Herskevych to “fight for truth, freedom and … remembrance”.

The Paralympics will take place from March 6 to March 15.
